attribution.note: Zitron directly asserts both the transparency criticism and the remote login requirement.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves both components. Providing credentials means entering them in a remote login session; it does not establish permanent password storage.

contract.note: The launch period, supported-service scope, and focus on founder-history disclosures are ordinary contextual readings. Requiring concrete omissions fairly operationalizes the transparency criticism.

evidence.note: Contemporary firsthand testing supports the ordinary remote credential-entry procedure. It does not establish historical omissions or exhaustively test authentication alternatives.
This earlier company disclosure distinguishes authentication from credential storage. It neither independently verifies security practices nor rebuts the described remote login procedure.
The later report identifies an asserted 2023 rebranding disclosure, relevant to what was public before the post. Rabbit's response does not establish completeness of historical disclosures.

reviews.rationale: The remote login component has contemporary support. The packet does not establish material historical omissions or sufficiently complete disclosures to settle the transparency component. Partial support with an unresolved component does not establish a mixed outcome.
